label: debug read-out
title: the top-left GPU pass timings / counts / guard states text (also ?hud); off keeps the corner for the interaction panel

label: quality preset
title: resolution cap / scale, beam steps, cache probe density, smoke solver iterations (also ?quality=verylow|low|medium|high|ultra)

label: adaptive resolution
title: steps the resolution scale down (at most every 2 s, in steps of at least 0.05) while the frame rate sits under ~45 fps and gives pixels back over ~58; the temporal histories are resampled across each step, so a step is neither a slow frame nor a flash

label: motion-calm rows (shipped on)
title: GI-in-motion lane (docs/internal/gi-motion.md §5, docs/review/gi-motion.html): the noise the picture shows IN MOTION is the direct chain's — ReSTIR's temporal reuse under a moving camera + the resolve's motion terms — and these are the rows of those two that measurably calm it: restir spatialAll + penRays, resolve motion α 0.4 → 0.25 and motion sharpen 0.3 → 0.15. Measured at high: −14 … −51 % of the pan flow per tile, the STILL tiles −28 … −55 % (spatial reuse halves ReSTIR's static crawl too), the daylight breach wall +7 %, ≈ +0.6 ms; the trades to look at: contact-shadow softness (spatial reuse everywhere) and motion sharpness (α 0.25). On by default (?nomotioncalm boots without it). Off = every row as the preset / defaults have it; re-applied after preset changes while on

label: fixed 60 Hz game step
title: the game stepped in whole 1/60 s ticks whatever the display's rate (host/loop.ts FIXEDSTEP; ON in the page, ?fixedstep=0 = off): the same simulation on a 60, a 120 and a 144 Hz display — groundwork for two-player co-op. Off = one update a frame on the frame's own time, as before. A script's __runFrames always names its own dt

label: draw between ticks
title: with the fixed step: a frame that falls between two game ticks is drawn at the blend of them (host/tween.ts TWEEN; ON in the page, ?tween=0 = off) — doors, props, debris, what the men carry, the men, carried lights and the camera (it steps with the tick too); sparks, tracers and laser lines are drawn as the last tick left them. The picture stands a constant part of a tick behind the game: none on a 60 Hz display, half a tick at 120 Hz, never more than one. Off = every frame draws the last tick: off 60 Hz the men and the camera move at 60 a second whatever the display draws

label: ladder: climb on GPU headroom
title: with adaptive resolution on: over 1-s windows in which the frame rate held the display rate AND the compute passes' GPU UNION stayed under 60 % of a 60-fps budget, three windows running, the ladder takes ONE step up — the render scale by 0.05 past the tier's start up to 0.95 (1.0 with sharp direct off), then (union under 65 %) the gather ⅓ → ½ res, then the volumetrics ¼ → ½ — at most one climb per 4 s; a window over 80 % of the budget or under 55 fps with a climb standing undoes the newest step at once and holds that rung off for a minute. Under auto a cheaper preset goes up a PRESET first; the climb spends what is left at the top. Needs GPU timestamp queries (it never acts without). Off = the ladder exactly as it was

label: ladder: frame rate to hold
title: the ONE target the quality ladder works to (also ?aim=asnow|60|90|120|display, ?aim=0 = asnow; needs adaptive resolution on). AS NOW: aims at a 60 Hz budget, spends GPU headroom on resolution and cuts only under 45 fps. HOLD N: the same climb against N's own GPU budget, but two 1-s windows under N (or the GPU over its band) cut the resolution straight to what the cost model says holds N — then the preset under auto — and pixels come back only on measured headroom. Never aims past the rate this display has been seen to show; a page paced by something other than the GPU is left alone. Trades resolution for frame rate. HOLD 60 is the default; AS NOW = the ladder before the aim
extra: as now / hold 60 / hold 90 / hold 120 / hold the display rate
aim ▸ hold 0 fps (display seen at 0 Hz) · gpu ∪ budget 0 ms

label: ladder: leave a paced page alone
title: AS NOW only (also ?ladderpaced=0). A page something else holds to a low frame rate — the browser's energy saver, a power mode, a slow display — is not helped by fewer pixels. ON: a slow frame more than twice its GPU work is never cut; a cut that bought no frame rate is taken straight back (preset too); and a resolution left low is given back as far as it provably costs nothing. OFF = the rule as it was: any slow page with the GPU union over 11 ms is cut, down to the floor.

label: ladder: an aim leaves a held page alone
title: UNDER AN AIM (hold 60 and up; also ?ladderheld=0). The same check as the row above, for the default ladder: on a page the browser holds to a low frame rate (energy saver on a low battery) the GPU clocks down and reads long, and fewer pixels buy no frame rate. ON: a slow frame far longer than its GPU work takes a test cut; if the frame is no shorter there the pixels come straight back and that rate is remembered as the page's pace (if it is shorter, the cut was real and stays). At the pace nothing is cut for the size of the GPU time and a resolution left low comes back a step at a time, each step checked. The pace is tested again every couple of minutes (a few seconds low). OFF = an aim as it was.

label: ladder: auto drops sharp direct before pixels
title: AUTO only (also ?laddershed=0). Sharp direct draws the geometry, the direct light and the composite at the full output size, so its cost does not shrink when the resolution does. ON: where auto would cut the resolution under the preset's own, or give the preset up, it turns sharp direct off first and the picture keeps its size; it stays off across auto's preset changes and comes back when the GPU time priced with it fits again (no sooner than a minute, longer each time it has to go again). OFF = the ladder as it was. A pinned preset keeps sharp direct either way.

extra: shed ▸ sharp direct off · not back for 0 s · it cost 0 ms he
climb ▸ 0 · roomy 0/3 · gpu ∪ 0 ms @ 0 fps · held off: 0

label: max internal height
title: the cap: internal render height in px at resolution scale 1.0 (the preset sets it — 1200 / 1000 / 900 / 720 / 600); a window shorter than this in device pixels renders its own height

label: resolution scale
title: RELATIVE TO THE CAP: internal height = min(max internal height, window height × dpr) × this — 1.0 = the cap, and every step down really renders fewer pixels (the read-out's res line shows the result); the adaptive ladder moves this same number and stops at 0.5

label: keep histories across resizes
title: a scale step / preset cap change / window resize resamples the direct-light, indirect and specular temporal histories into the new targets and recycles render targets through a pool (no reallocation, no first-touch clears, no restart flash); a gather- or beam-divisor flip re-creates only the targets on that grid. Off = the old path: everything reallocated, every history restarted (for A/B)

label: histories
extra: [restart screen histories — zero every screen-space history (direct light, indirect, specular, the resolve, the reservoirs): the next frame accumulates from raw estimates as after a cold boot — the A/B for what carrying them buys (watch a soft shadow or the bounce light for the frame after)]

label: debug view
title: the renderer's buffers, one at a time, in place of the final picture (this list is the only way to them: no key steps through them). 16 = the gather's resampling reservoirs (ultra, phase 5): red = confidence M ÷ cap, green = the temporal history was found and taken, blue = spatial taps accepted ÷ k — the plain indirect with resampling off; 17 = the reflection pass's output as composite fetches it, before the cutoff fade (mesh hits / hit-lighting reuse are judged here). 14 = the ray-traced reflections' term by itself (renderer v3 phase 4; black with the pass off); 15 = the g-buffer's material: red = roughness (bright = matte), green = metalness — the finish table plus the detail layer's wear. 11 / 12 = the ReSTIR estimator per pixel: history M ÷ cap per class (r / g) + tile gradient resets (b), then rays ÷ 6 (r) / spatial taps (g) / classes shaded from a neighbour (b). 13 = the v3 shadow client per pixel: red / green = σ of the sharp / broad class (the filtered sample variance — lit only in penumbrae), blue = the sharp class's history length (dark = fresh / moving light, bright = long still history). specular = the glossy-floor reflection term and / or what the glass panes add (mirror + glints + dust), alone — whichever is on; black elsewhere. The albedo view washes pixels behind glass faintly teal so the panes can be found
extra: final / albedo / normals / direct light / indirect light / volumetrics / depth / cache irradiance (dice) / lighting only / denoiser blur hints / specular (gloss + glass + RT) / restir: history / gradient / restir: rays / taps / denoiser state (v3 shadow client) / RT reflections alone / material (rough / metal) / (16: free) / RT raw (phase 5)

label: fxaa
title: the final blit's edge AA — only WITHOUT TAAU (under the temporal resolve the blit sharpens instead; this box then does nothing)

label: dither
title: ±½ LSB triangular noise against 8-bit banding

label: TAAU (temporal AA + upsampling)
title: render at the internal size under a sub-pixel jitter and resolve every frame into an OUTPUT-resolution history (the cap's rows) that the bloom / tonemap / a sharpen then read: antialiased edges, the stochastic lighting noise averaged down, and fewer pixels rendered for the same canvas. Off = no jitter, canvas = internal size, FXAA (?notaau at boot). The render scale is left where it is — a preset applies its own (ultra 0.9 · high 0.77 · medium 0.67 · low 0.6 · verylow 0.5 with TAAU, 1.0 without)

label: taau: new-frame weight
title: base share of THIS frame in the resolved pixel where nothing moved (0.1 ≈ ten frames of memory); the resolve raises it by itself where the history had to be clipped, where things move fast, and where particles / rain were drawn

label: taau: clip γ
title: history clip box = the frame's 3×3 neighbourhood mean ± γ·σ (YCoCg): tight (1.0) converges lighting changes fast and ghosts least, loose (1.5+) is smoother / less flicker but trails

label: taau: jitter phases
title: Halton(2,3) cycle length: 8 for mild ratios, 16 for the deep upscales; 0 = no jitter (for A/B: the resolve then only blurs an aliased picture in time)

label: taau: sharpen
title: contrast-adaptive sharpen (RCAS-style, no halo by construction) in the final blit — the resolve's reconstruction kernel is a little soft on purpose

label: taau: reactive ×
title: how hard the particles' mask and the rain's share of a pixel push it toward this frame (0 = ignore: sparks surface at a tenth of their brightness and trail, rain streaks melt into mist)

label: taau: kernel k
title: current-frame reconstruction w = exp(−|d|²·k), d in output px: 2 ≈ σ 0.5 px; higher = sharper per frame, more aliasing carried into the history

label: taau: MOTION new-frame weight (0 = off)
title: motion sharpness (docs/internal/tjank.md §vi): a pixel that reprojected half an output pixel or more this frame (camera or object; ramping in from an eighth) takes the new frame at this weight instead of α — the history is resampled at ANY fractional offset, so the softening does not wait for fast motion — a resampled history is a blur in motion, and noise in motion reads far less than blur. 0.25 shipped (the motion-calm rows; 0.4 with them off); 0 = the old rule (0.25 at 24 px / frame)

label: taau: MOTION sharpen boost
title: what the final blit's contrast-adaptive sharpen gains while the CAMERA moves (the largest screen motion of five points round its look-at, full at half an output pixel a frame): sharpen + this. 0.15 shipped (0.3 with the motion-calm rows off); 0 = off

label: taau: motion → weight
title: how much fast on-screen motion (24 px/frame = full) raises the new-frame weight toward 0.25 — less smear in a pan, more aliasing

label: taau
extra: [drop history — the next resolve takes the frame outright, as after a cut]

label: taau: history de-blur (motion)
title: C2: while a pixel is being resampled (motion) the fetched history gains this × (Catmull-Rom − bilinear at the same spot) — the band each resample eats — before the clip; 0 = off

label: motion identity (keyed dynamic boxes)
title: the motion vectors of leaves, furniture, thrown items, hand props and devices come from the transform the SAME part had last frame wherever it sat in the dynamic list (a spawn / despawn no longer hands everything after it a wrong vector for a frame); off = the g-buffer index-matches by size + owner as before

label: SHARP DIRECT (native-res U + composite)
title: under TAAU at a render scale below 1: rasterise the g-buffer, evaluate every light's exact unshadowed contribution and run the composite + TAA at the OUTPUT size; keep the shadow ratio, the bounce, the reflections and the volumetric march at the internal size and joint-bilateral upsample them — light pools, cone edges, box edges and decals go native-sharp, penumbrae stay soft. Off = every pass as it was (?nosharp)

label: GBAA (analytic box-edge AA, single frame)
title: geometry-buffer anti-aliasing: the g-buffer writes each pixel's signed distance to the nearest edge of the box face it shows; before the resolve every pixel an edge crosses is blended with its neighbour across the edge by exact coverage — clean box edges with NO history and no jitter (pair with taau: jitter phases 0 to make the TAA a pure noise pass); characters, glass and intersection lines stay the resolve's. Off = no pass (the frame as it was)

label: sharp: DECOUPLED jitter (still output raster, jittered internal)
title: under sharp direct: the output raster (geometry, U, composite, GBAA, the 1 : 1 resolve) runs unjittered while the internal raster the shadow ratio / bounce / reflections live on keeps its ±½ px Halton jitter — hard shadow edges computed at internal resolution settle smooth in the resolve instead of stair-stepping, and the geometry stays rock still for GBAA. Off = one jitter for both (as it was)

label: sharp: SLIVER rule
title: an output pixel none of whose 4×4 internal texels lies on its own surface (a door reveal, a chair leg, a limb's edge — 0.01–0.02 % of a frame at the follow camera) has no measured visibility: rule 0 borrowed the neighbours' ratio whatever surface they show (a lit floor lent lit to an occluded sliver: thin bright lines), per channel (their hue with it); rule 1 borrows nothing across surfaces — one deterministic ray per class to the strongest live emitter from the output pixel, the remainder on the neighbours' luminance ratio, both classes alike (docs/internal/direct-quality.md)
extra: 0 borrow the 2×2 (as it was) / 1 same-surface only + a ray

label: sharp: sliver rays per tile (cap)
title: per 8×8 output tile at most this many sliver pixels trace their ray (ranked in lane order); 0 = no rays (the conservative remainder rule for the whole class, and the tracer-free kernel)

label: GBAA: same-surface clamp
title: blend an edge pixel toward the neighbour across its edge only when that neighbour is at or behind it — never toward a NEARER third surface standing over the edge (a man before a partition's top edge lent half his colour to every edge pixel his outline crossed). Off = Persson's blend as it was

label: sharp: same-plane k
title: the ratio upsample's same-plane weight e^(−plane distance ∕ (view distance · k)) (0.01)

label: hour
title: the level at another hour: a sun in the moon's place, the sky, haze and exposure of that hour, the outside lamps on a photocell (out at midday and under overcast), the night's storm held off. Night = the level exactly as it was made. The same pick as ?hour= and the mission sheet's Hour row; the AI's light meter reads the same sun and sky.
extra: Dawn / Midday / Grey day / Dusk / Night

label: sun strength
title: the hour's sun at this share of its own strength (1) — the one number a cloud dims: the picture's light and the light meter's stand-in read the same value. Moved by hand it STAYS where it is put, whatever the weather (the button below hands it back). Nothing at night.

label: sun
extra: [back to the weather's cloud — a sun strength set by hand, handed back: under a picked weather the sun stands where its cloud puts it, with none at the hour's own]

label: exposure
title: linear gain before the AgX curve (default 2.0)

label: bloom
title: fraction of the blurred HDR frame added back before tonemapping (no threshold: every pixel scatters a little, bright ones visibly)

label: saturation
title: AgX look: 1 = neutral AgX (rather grey), 1.15 default

label: indirect scale
title: multiplies the final-gather bounce on screen only (light meter / AI unaffected). 1 = physical, 0.35 default look

label: emissive scale
title: brightness of emissive fixtures AND of the area lights derived from them

label: night vision tube gain
title: log gain of the intensifier: signal = log(1+L·g)/log(1+g)

label: night vision phosphor
title: 0 = white phosphor (P45, modern), 1 = classic green (P43); default 0.09 = white with a touch of green

label: night vision eyepiece edge
title: the dark oval round the goggles' picture: 0 = none (default), 1 = the oval as it was (?nvoval=1)

label: film grain
title: display-space grain, faded out of highlights

label: enabled
title: sampled ray-traced direct light: every light scored per pixel, the strongest per emitter class get shadow rays to points on their emitters

label: restir: HYBRID — held-light rays K (0 = off)
title: THE HYBRID ESTIMATOR: every light a character CARRIES (owner byte ≠ 0: the guards' torches, the player's rail / gun light, muzzle flashes, tracer heads) bypasses the reservoirs at the pixels it reaches and gets the old leader treatment every frame — the two strongest at the pixel take K stratified emitter samples each, shaded exactly, any further ones one tail ray a class; static lights (owner 0) keep ReSTIR. A carried light moves every frame, so its reservoir history and the shadow client's ratio history are let go wherever the cone sweeps and the pool was shaded from one or two fresh rays: noisy pools, ragged edges, rims. The presets tier K (ultra 8 · high 4 · medium 4 · low 3 · verylow 2); 0 = off, the transient stratum exactly as it was (docs/internal/direct-quality.md)

label: TRADE: held rays stop at 2 if agreed
title: a carried light's first two stratified rays that agree (both lit, both blocked) stand for all K: 2 rays instead of K inside the cone and behind walls, the full K where they differ. Cost: its wide penumbrae harden a little and grain more (a pixel 90 % lit reads about 94 %), and an occluder thinner than the lens spread can be missed by both rays. Needs K above 2.

label: TRADE: settled pixels re-trace 1 in 2
title: a reservoir sample that is fully lit, with most of its memory and no penumbra measured at the pixel last frame, is re-traced on alternate frames only (the fresh candidates still look every frame). Cost: a shadow arriving on a settled lit pixel can show a frame late along its leading edge.

label: TRADE: dim class
title: share of the pixel's light; 0 = off. An emitter class (sharp / broad) under this share of the pixel's live unshadowed light takes one shadow ray a frame (re-trace and fresh alternate) and no second penumbra ray. Cost: grain in that class, worst where the bright class is itself in shadow. Try 0.05.

label: restir: shadow rays / pixel
title: 2 = each class alternates re-tracing its history sample and tracing a fresh candidate (flipping checkerboard) · 3 = both classes re-trace, one fresh candidate alternates · 4 = re-trace + fresh for both classes · 5 = + a final visibility ray when spatial reuse picks a neighbour's sample (spatial reuse then runs everywhere) · 6 = + a second fresh candidate per class. Presets: ultra 4 · high 4 · medium 4 · low 3 · verylow 2 (5 and 6 measured dearer than they are worth: this slider keeps them for A/B)

label: restir: spatial taps
title: neighbour reservoirs combined per pixel (pairwise MIS, plane / normal rejection) — below 5 rays only where the pixel's own history is young (see 'young M'), at 5+ everywhere with a final visibility ray. 0 = temporal reuse only. Presets 5 / 3 / 2 / 2 / 1

label: restir: history M cap
title: temporal confidence cap in candidate-equivalents: 20 ≈ a 20-frame memory where nothing changes. Big visibility / lighting changes are caught at once by the target-ratio rule and the tile gradient regardless; this sets the steady-state smoothness vs the convergence rate of SMALL changes

label: restir: spatial radius (px @1000 rows)
title: disc the spatial taps are drawn from (scaled with the internal resolution, never wider than ~0.6 m on the surface)

label: restir: tile gradient confidence
title: per 8×8 tile: the sum of this frame's fresh one-sample estimates vs the sum of the temporal ones, per class — when they disagree by more than the threshold (a shadow sweeping in or out, a door letting light in, a man stepping in front of a lamp) the tile's history confidence drops to 0 within the frame instead of the estimate converging at the M cap's rate. Off = plain capped reuse (A/B: watch the trailing edge of a walking man's shadow)

label: restir: gradient threshold z
title: the tile's paired z statistic — mean (fresh − temporal) over the lanes that have both, in units of its own sampling spread — under which the history keeps full confidence; none past 1.6× it. 5 default (3.5 until 08-11: the street lamp's patch on the floor behind the cubicles' windows — one rarely-visible light dominating the tile's weight, fat-tailed z — reset 1–2 % of its tiles a frame there and crawled): a shadow edge or a door moves dozens of lanes the same way (z ≫ 5), the steady state sits at |z| ~ 1 whatever the light level (lower = quicker but twitchier)

label: restir: young M (spatial below 5 rays)
title: without the final ray (rays < 5) a neighbour's visibility stands in for this pixel's, which softens hard shadow edges by up to the radius — so spatial reuse only runs where this pixel's history is younger than this (just disoccluded / reset: noisy anyway, and the bias lasts a few frames). 0 = never below 5 rays; 30 = always

label: restir: known-dark lights leave the draw
title: the lights an 8×8 tile's own shadow rays found dark EVERYWHERE last frame (a street lamp behind the outer wall, the next room's panel behind a shut door — in the unshadowed total, reach level > 0, never visible) leave that tile's fresh candidate draw: known dark like a reach-masked light — no ray, and none of the one-sample all-or-nothing noise that made the dim end of the break-room lino crawl (restir.wgsl BELIEFS). Off = A/B the first cut: every live light in the draw (unbiased; the auditors below then have nothing to do)

label: restir: audit fraction
title: on this share of a tile's frames (spread over every 64, staggered across tiles) EVERY lane of an 8×8 tile that holds some light dark spends one extra shadow ray re-testing one of them (drawn by unshadowed weight; the outcome only votes — whole tiles at once, because a SIMD group half-filled with audit rays pays for all of them). A light lit anywhere in the 5×5 tiles round a tile never leaves its draw, so moving shadow edges need no audit; this is what overturns a verdict for a light arriving where nothing near had it lit (a door starting to open on the next room's panel): 0 = only the reservoirs that hold a light lit can, 1 = every frame (a ray per lane per frame)

label: restir: hue split (a sample of an unbelieved light keeps its own hue)
title: the believed-visible mix colours only the luminance its own lights carried; the share of the estimate carried by a sample whose light this pixel does not believe visible (tile-dark here, or its own darkSlot) keeps that sample's hue — without it a blocked light's penumbra deep in its own shadow was painted in whatever far dim light the tile still believed: coloured fringes along shadow boundaries under two lights of different colour (docs/internal/direct-quality.md S3). Off = the belief hue as it was

label: restir: D1 second fresh ray inside penumbrae
title: a second fresh candidate + shadow ray per class in penumbra pixels whatever the tier's ray count (+1 ray where the estimate is uncertain; an auditing tile's penumbra lanes give up their audit slot that frame). On by default through the motion-calm rows

label: restir: spatial everywhere (biased)
title: spatial reuse at every pixel even without the final visibility ray: contact shadows soften by up to the radius. ON by default through Frame ▸ Quality & resolution ▸ motion-calm rows; off = only where the visibility ray runs

label: restir: motion — stochastic-bilinear reprojection
title: under a camera pan the temporal reservoir used to come from the NEAREST texel to the reprojected point: at 2.4 px a frame every pixel inherits from 2 px back while the picture moved 2.4, so the reservoir pattern slides across the floor the TAA holds still and neighbouring pixels share one verdict — 2–7-px blotches crawling under a panning floor. On: the texel is one of the four round the reprojected point, drawn by its bilinear weight per pixel per frame and validated by depth as ever, so a lineage follows the surface (diffusing ± ½ px) instead. Inert at rest by construction (docs/internal/direct-motion.md)

label: restir: motion — motion-scaled confidence
title: the reservoir's memory (M cap) at a pixel shrinks with that pixel's own screen motion — whole under the 'full-confidence motion' below, down to the floor past 1.6 × it: a panning pixel leans on fresh candidates, whose error is white frame to frame (the ratio filter and the TAA average it), instead of on a history reprojected to the nearest texel from somewhere else; the full memory the moment it rests. Measured at high: a 0.8-px-a-frame pan keeps ReSTIR's history worth all 20 candidates (any cut costs 10–25 % more flow), a 1.4–2-px walking pan about two (docs/internal/direct-motion.md)

label: restir: motion — full-confidence motion (px @1000 rows)
title: screen motion per frame, in px at 1000 internal rows (scaled to the target), under which a pixel's reservoir keeps its whole memory; the cut ramps to the floor by 1.6 × this (1.1: high's walking pan of ~2 px sits past the ramp, a slow creep of 0.8 px before it)

label: restir: motion — confidence floor
title: the least fraction of the M cap a fast-moving pixel keeps (0.1 = a 2-candidate memory at cap 20)

label: restir: motion — spatial reuse under motion
title: the spatial taps run at every pixel moving faster than the threshold below (spatial-everywhere only where the history is being handed about anyway; nothing extra at rest — moot while 'A/B spatial everywhere' is on)

label: restir: motion — spatial threshold (px @1000 rows)
title: screen motion per frame, in px at 1000 internal rows (scaled to the target), past which the spatial pass opens at the pixel with the tap count below

label: restir: motion — spatial taps under motion
title: the tap count at a moving pixel when it is above the tier's own (0 = the tier's k): the fresh candidates a cut-down history leans on are one or two rays a pixel — the neighbours' reservoirs are the rest of the samples, and taps trace no rays. Costs only while the picture moves

label: denoiser
title: master switch for temporal + spatial (off = raw samples, for inspection)

label: mesh-traced character shadows (ultra: every ray · high: near receivers)
title: every shadow / occlusion ray (this pass, the gather's hit shading, cascade hits, beams, the light probes) tests characters against their SKINNED TRIANGLE MESH — per character a BVH over the shared mannequin topology, re-skinned and refit bottom-up in two small compute dispatches a frame ("mesh" in the read-out) and walked stacklessly per ray after the bounding-sphere cull — instead of the 15 fitted round-cone proxies: arms, hands, shins, feet and the head cast their real silhouettes, and the rays the proxies block that the body does not (~17 % for the old capsules, tools/qa/mesh-shadow-ref.ts; about half that for the fitted cones) come through. Primary visibility and closest-hit shading of characters are untouched (self-shadow: the SDF character rig section's row). Measured (M4 Max, 2133×1200 ultra, four men, a torch point-blank on a crouched player): skin+refit 0.13 ms, direct / gather / volumetrics level or slightly cheaper than the proxy path. Off = the round-cone proxies, every other preset's path (frame flag 8388608; also ?meshShadows)

label: · mesh shadows: NEAR receivers only (high's form)
title: with mesh shadows on: a shadow ray walks a man's mesh only when it STARTS within 0.6 m of his cull sphere — the floor at his boots, the desk under his hand, the man beside him, his own pixels — and takes his round cones from anywhere farther (common.wgsl meshShadowT, frame.rigCfg bit 128). The mesh is what closes the lit 1–2 px seam between a rasterised limb and the shadow its slimmer proxy casts beside it, a contact defect; a torch throwing him on a wall 3 m off reads alike off either — and the every-ray walk cost 0.9 ms of direct light in a four-man torch corridor at high where this costs a tenth of it. HIGH ships it on (with mesh shadows); ultra walks the mesh for every ray (off); no effect while mesh shadows are off

label: light reach masks
title: each static interior light carries a CPU-built mask of the level cells it can possibly reach past full-height walls (reach.ts); a walled-off light is skipped at a pixel instead of stealing a leader slot from the room's own dim lights (the dark break room's hard coloured arcs) — off = every light competes everywhere, for A/B

label: moonlight
title: the level's moon. At a day hour (Frame ▸ Hour) the moon is out and the sun stands in its place: the slider then only sets what the moon comes back at

label: torch / unit light intensity
title: every carried torch and every spawned unit's weapon light (teammates, scenario defenders, the response team)

label: your light intensity
title: your own rail light, on whichever gun is in your hands

label: sky brightness
title: × the sky as the hour and the weather last set it. When either changes the sky (Frame ▸ Hour, a weather's cloud) this reads 1 again and the next move scales the new sky

label: torch bounce cards (analytic torch bounce)
title: every carried spot light (the guards' torches and weapon lights, the player's rail light) gets its FOOTPRINT on the surface its beam hits rebuilt each frame as a one-sided analytic emitter — a tiny compute pass traces the axis and 64 cone samples: claim disc, flux-weighted centroid and radius, radiance × area from the flux that really landed there × the paint it landed on — and the final gather takes that patch's bounce analytically with one shadow ray instead of hoping its four cosine rays find a 30 cm hotspot; rays that do land in the footprint drop that light's direct term there, so nothing counts twice. The boiling bounce round a torch near a wall goes by construction (and the firefly bound below stops eating that bounce). Off = no card pass, nothing sampled or excluded: bit-identical (frame flag 33554432; docs/internal/perf-2026-08-10.md)

label: firefly bound × cache
title: final gather: each ray ≤ K × the radiance cache's irradiance at the point ÷ π (outlier rejection against the local light field: kills the boiling round a torch near a wall, at the price of some bounce within ~0.6 m of an intense hotspot); 0 = off = the old absolute clamp only. Set by the quality preset (4; ultra 0) — a value moved here sticks until the next preset change

label: temporal accumulation
title: reprojected, depth-validated, variance-clipped history on the half-res indirect only (also drives the cache jitter/EMA); direct light has its own knob (Direct light ▸ Shadow rays & penumbra filter ▸ temporal reuse); beams never use history

label: multi-bounce
title: hit points read the cached irradiance volume → light keeps bouncing

label: LOSSY: gather at 1/3 res (not 1/2)
title: final gather, its temporal accumulation and the à-trous run at a third of the internal resolution (4/9 of the pixels of half res); fgather / temporal / giblur / the composite upsample read the divisor from frame.lossyCfg.x and the targets are recreated when it changes. Off = the half-res path untouched

label: glossy floors (RT reflections off)
title: Does nothing while Materials ▸ RT reflections is on (ultra / high / medium): that pass replaces it. Traced glossy reflections on the polished floors (lobby stone, corridor + break-room lino — BoxFlag.Gloss): the final gather spends ONE extra mirror ray per gloss texel (view direction reflected about the floor, jittered over a 2.5° cone), shades what it hits like a gather hit plus the fixture's own glow (lit panels, screens, beacon domes, windows onto the sky, a torch spot on the wall), weights it by Schlick Fresnel on the view angle (F0 0.04 → ~0.045 from up here) × 0.85, runs it through its own half-res history + one blur pass and adds it in composite AFTER the diffuse terms (never × albedo). Costs about one trace + one shadow ray per gloss texel at gather res (shows in "gather") and two half-res filter dispatches (in "temporal"). Off = nothing stored, filtered or read: bit-identical (frame flag 2097152; debug view "specular" shows the term alone)

label: probe density
title: read one bounce away from the eye, so density barely shows through the gather

label: base interval (m)
title: cascade n traces [L·(4ⁿ−1)/3, L·(4ⁿ⁺¹−1)/3]

label: stagger upper cascades
title: update c2+ every other frame (every fourth with the half-rate option below)

label: LOSSY: cache at half rate
title: upper cascades trace on even frames, c0 + the dice bake on odd ones (one direction jitter per pair, so merges and the bake stay consistent); the dice volume the gather / composite / volumetrics / light meter read is at most one frame older. Resting levels report an honest 0 ms to the HUD on their off frame. Off = every cascade every frame, untouched

label: amortized upkeep (schedule on)
title: ON: each upper cascade level re-traces an interleaved 1/period of its probes per frame per the schedule below (constant work every frame; c0 + the dice bake always whole; a rebuilt cache primes with whole bakes and a history-free first dice bake). With the schedule at [1,1,1,1] it dispatches exactly what it always did. OFF = every level whole every frame through the original dispatch, whatever the schedule says

label: LOSSY: refresh schedule [c0,c1,c2,c3]
title: frames each level takes to refresh all its probes (the preset writes this; c0 is always whole). Far-field light (> 3 m from a probe for c2, > 12.6 m for c3) then lands over that many frames — under the dice EMA's own ~7-frame settle
extra: whole every frame [1,1,1,1] (ultra / high) / far field over 2 / 4 frames [1,1,2,4] (medium) / [1,2,3,6] (low) / [1,2,4,8] (verylow) / stress: [1,4,8,16]

label: occupancy split [–,c1,c2,c3]
title: workgroups per upper-cascade probe — the same output bits for any value, only the cost moves (1/1/2/8 measured best on the M4 Max: cascades 1.77 → 1.05 ms; 1/1/1/1 = the original one-workgroup-per-probe dispatch)

label: probe visibility weights
title: ray-traced probe visibility when merging cascades (thin-wall leak fix)

label: volumetric beams
title: in-scattered light from spot/point lights in the thin haze (equi-angular, shadow-rayed)

label: haze density
title: uniform thin haze that makes light beams visible

label: LOSSY: volumetrics at 1/4 res (not 1/2)
title: haze beams + smoke march on a quarter-res target (each texel marches one pixel of its 4×4 block, interleaved), composited with the same depth-aware 3×3 upsample scaled to the texel spacing; frame.lossyCfg.y carries the divisor, the target is recreated on change. Off = the half-res path untouched

label: CAP: lights per smoke step / haze ray
title: the volumetric worst-case cap: at most K lights get a shadow ray per smoke-march step (the first K, in order of their unshadowed bound on that stretch of the ray, that reach the step) / per haze view ray (the K beams with the largest unshadowed in-scatter, sharing a step budget by it), the rest dropped. THE lever on what the march costs. Set by the quality preset (high 4 · medium, low and very low 2); a value moved here sticks until the next preset change

label: CAP: smoke shadow ray every N steps
title: each traced light's shadow ray + self-shadow march is refreshed every N march steps and reused between (a step is 8 cm of a 5.5 cm-voxel plume). 2 on every preset (1 = every step: nothing visible gained, a third dearer); 3 starts to comb shadow edges inside a plume

label: CAP: smoke march step (voxels)
title: the smoke march step in voxels of the domain being walked (1.5 on high, medium and low; 2+ combs the shadow edges inside a plume: very low only)

label: smoke shadows
title: shadow rays are attenuated by smoke volumes (lights dim behind a cloud)

label: calm: wait, frames
title: the longest a brick whose air is slow waits between steps (it then takes the time it missed); how slow is the CALM row below (cells crossed in the wait). 1 = every brick every frame

label: calm: far, cells
title: the CALM row's allowance for bricks far from where the camera looks (past "view: near m"); 0 = no laxer than in sight

label: reads hop over clear air
title: shadow rays and the view march skip stretches the page says hold nothing; same samples either way. Off (as it ships: it bought no time on the Mac) = asked brick by brick

label: fresh smoke share
title: the share of the pool thin old smoke may never take: as the pool fills its last 2 × this, haze is refused bricks, keeps less air round it and fades sooner, so a can just thrown stands up. 0 = first come

label: gun gas: fade /s
title: thin smoke on the fine lattice (gun gas) fades this much faster, always: the crisp gas at the muzzle is untouched, the haze it spreads into gives its bricks back. 0 = a magazine on AUTO takes two thirds of the pool and hangs as a veil

label: gun gas: pool share
title: what the fine lattice may hold of the pool when canister smoke wants the rest (it has more while nobody else does): haze is refused bricks from 0.7 of it, everything but a muzzle at all of it. 1 = no share

label: view: bias
title: far from where the camera looks the pool's ceiling starts sooner and bites harder; 0 = one ceiling everywhere

label: view: near m
title: inside this of the look-at point smoke is near; far is full at twice it

label: ceiling from fill
title: the share of the pool from which thin smoke everywhere starts to fade faster (full at 0.95)

label: air round smoke
title: cells of clear air simulated round the smoke (8 = all 26 neighbour bricks)

label: idle brick, steps
title: steps a brick nothing needs is held before its slot goes back (never under 8 while bricks may wait)

label: whole pool from
title: read only while the solver goes by the GPU-written count (?smokeindirect=1, a software adapter, the F8 row while it is flipped): the share of the pool stepping from which the whole pool is dispatched instead; over 1 = never. A page on a real card opens on the whole pool and does not read this

extra: bricks 0 (0 sitting this frame out) · scalar 0 · render 0 ·

label: CALM bricks: voxels per visible step
title: a brick whose air is slow steps every p-th frame (1, 2 or 4: the Smoke pool section's "calm: wait" row is the longest) with the dt it sat out added on: between two steps you see, its smoke never moves more than this many voxels. A source wakes what it reaches, and a brick never waits longer than any of its 26 neighbours. 0 = every brick in view every frame (out of view the "calm: far, cells" row still holds; "calm: wait" 1 = nothing ever waits)

label: shadow rays: smoke samples
title: samples a SHADOW ray takes through 3.5 m of smoke (the direct pass, gather / reflection / probe-meter hits) — 8 = the estimator as it always was; 6 saves ~0.2 ms of the direct pass with three plumes up, 4 ~0.4 but blotches the plume's shadow on the floor (docs/internal/smoke-perf.md §4). The plume you look at (the volumetric march) and the guards' sight lines never read this

label: pressure: rb pairs
title: red-black Gauss-Seidel + over-relaxation: red/black sweep pairs per step (2 dispatches each; the quality preset sets it)

label: render density × (gun smoke / dust)
title: the render density every reader takes for what is NOT canister smoke — muzzle gas, impact puffs, destruction dust; kept per cell, so it acts on smoke already in the air (the row below is the plumes' own ×; 1.0 = as those effects were tuned)

label: render density ×
title: CANISTER PLUMES: the density every reader sees — the march, the shadow rays and the guards' sight-line probe alike (1.3 since 08-14: the blind-pairs winner in motion — 1.6 was the pick in stills, 1.0 the old renderer's)

label: multiple scattering (glow through the plume)
title: the march's second scattering octave (vol_common.wgsl smokeMsGain): the lit side's coloured glow carried THROUGH an opaque plume with half the extinction and a rounder phase — structure inside a thick plume. 0 = single scattering (the 08-14 ship set: off beat on in the blind pairs)

label: upsample: let go of the depth guide inside smoke
title: composite's depth-guided upsample of the half-res volumetrics drops its depth term where the texel is mostly SMOKE — a plume in front of a cabinet and of the floor beside it is the same smoke; guiding by the surface behind carved its edge along every depth edge (blind pairs: on beat off)

label: TAAU: smoke pixels reactive ×
title: a plume has no motion vectors — by (1 − its transmittance) × this the resolve leans on the fresh march instead of a stale plume clamped into place (0.3 default; higher = crisper billows in motion but the march's own dither shows, 0 = the smoothest and laggiest)

label: diffusion: starts at optical depth
title: under this optical depth the smoke diffusion leaves what is behind the plume alone — a plume's thin edge keeps the vending art crisp (0.35; the 08-12 build used 0.15 and smeared the art along the whole outline)

label: smoke blurs what is behind it
title: SMOKE DIFFUSION (post.wgsl): what you see THROUGH a plume is forward-scattered — blurred toward the frame's quarter / eighth-size copies by the smoke transmittance of the pixel's ray. 0 = attenuation only, edges pixel-crisp through any smoke (as it was)

label: curl round a moving body ×
title: THE LOOK PAGE, with its Stirred smoke row up: how many times MORE the solver keeps an eddy turning right round a man who is moving through smoke (0 = no more than anywhere else). Nothing anywhere else

label: canister density /s
title: applies to canisters that start emitting after the change

label: canister heat
title: buoyancy source: low = smoke hugs the floor and spreads, high = rises to the ceiling

label: RT reflections (replaces glossy floors)
title: ray-traced reflections on every surface whose finish is smooth enough (Box.rough per material in the level file — the office: lobby stone 0.15, lino 0.22, screens 0.08, brushed metal 0.28, the wet lot 0.22 anisotropic …; docs/internal/p4-materials.md): reflect.wgsl samples a GGX visible normal per pixel (Heitz 2018) at the g-buffer's per-pixel roughness, traces the reflected ray through the box grid + the character proxies like a gather ray, shades the hit (lit panels / signs / screens return their own radiance — the crisp shapes in the floor; anything else shadow-rayed direct + the cache's bounce; the sky on a miss), adds the analytic GGX highlight of every torch / lamp lens and rough-receiver panel through the same lobe, then the shared denoiser's SPECULAR client (per-pixel roughness: mirror-image reprojection, roughness-scaled clamp / cap, a lobe-footprint à-trous = contact hardening) settles it and composite adds it × the cutoff fade. REPLACES the glossy-floors row while on. Presets: ultra ÷2 · 2 rays · ≤ 0.55, high ÷2 · 1 · ≤ 0.45, medium ÷3 · 1 · ≤ 0.35, low / verylow off. Costs "reflect" + "rdenoise" in the debug read-out. Off = no dispatch, nothing read: bit-identical (frame.rtCfg.w = 0; ?nortreflect)

label: · RT target divisor
title: the reflection target's resolution: full internal res, half (ultra / high) or a third (medium); composite blends the four texels round a pixel for the mirror and nine for the lamps' highlights, each by how like its own surface the pixel's is, and fades both by the finish's roughness about the pixel. Re-makes the reflection targets (pooled; their histories resampled)

label: · RT rays per pixel
title: GGX-VNDF samples traced per reflecting pixel per frame (1 high, 2 ultra; 0 = the analytic highlights of the lights only, nothing traced — what the low tiers could afford); each is a full trace + a shadow ray at the hit, so "reflect" scales with it

label: · RT max roughness
title: finishes rougher than this get no ray of the mirror; the mirror fades out over the 0.12 under it so the cutoff never bands (0.45 high: floors, screens, metal; 0.55 ultra: + laminate and varnished wood; 0.35 medium: floors, screens, steel). The lamps' highlights do not go by this: they are drawn on every finish up to 0.5 and fade out to 0.75, on every preset

label: · RT à-trous iterations
title: iterations of the reflection chain's edge-aware blur after its temporal step (strides 1 2 4 8): each tap is bounded by the lobe's own footprint (α · hit distance ÷ view distance — sharp at a contact, soft further up), stops at geometry / a different roughness / a texel with no term, and its luminance stop is scaled by the temporal variance

label: · RT history cap (frames)
title: the specular client's history cap: the ROUGHEST finishes keep this many frames, a polish ~6 whatever it says (its image must track a walking man's torch), lino ¾ of it; more = smoother rough reflections that follow a moving light more slowly (a swung torch still converges in a few frames: the clamp shortens the history by how far it had to move it)

label: · RT wet-lot anisotropy
title: the wet asphalt's lobe stretched along the view direction (across × (1 − 0.6a), along × (1 + 5a)): 0 = isotropic — the sodium lamp mirrors as a disc; 0.7 = a long streak running toward the camera, as standing water on tarmac does. Only boxes with an anisotropic finish (the storm sets it on the lot) listen

label: · wet ground break-up
title: wet ground is pools in the low spots and damp aggregate between them (detail.wgsl wetGround: roughness +0.04 in a pool, +0.15 on the stone, so the reflection is patchy — bright in the pools, dull between); 0 = one even film of water, the wet lot as it was (?nowetbreak)

label: · lasers & tracers in reflections
title: a weapon laser's beam (either band, when it is drawn at all) and a tracer's streak show in the ray-traced reflections: the nearest 8 handed to the reflection pass as line segments, their mirror image analytic (reflect.wgsl beamImage; its strength is BEAM_REFL_MIN there); picture only — off = the pass as it was (?nobeamreflect)

label: · squad lasers as light in the air
title: the squad's weapon lasers are drawn as light scattered in the air: a thin line, faint in clear air and brighter in haze, smoke and rain, a dot that blooms where it lands, a glint at the emitter. off (?nobeamair) = the opaque glowing boxes as they were. picture only

label: · wet ground mirrors the men
title: on wet ground the ray-traced reflections take the share the simpler gloss of the low presets always had, so a lit man shows in the wet under him; a laser drawn as light in the air mirrors by that same share. Off = as it was

label: · RT strength
title: × the whole reflection term in composite (1 = as traced — physically it should stay there; the slider is for A/B by eye)

label: · analytic highlights
title: × the GGX image of the point / spot lenses, (on rough receivers) the lit panels and, on the look's page, the sun or the moon, on every finish under the cutoff — the primary-hit specular response to the level's lights: a torch swung across the lino is a gliding elongated highlight, the street lamp a streak in the wet lot (1 = physical; 0 = the traced term only)

label: detail layer
title: physically-explainable wear at the primary hit (gbuffer.wgsl detailSurface — no image textures, no painted noise): worn paths on the polished floors where the shift walks and at every threshold (rougher, a touch duller — the level's traffic map, render/wear.ts), grime in the band the mop misses along every wall foot, scuffed skirting on the bottom hand-width of walls and cabinets, dust on tops above eye level (rougher, greyer, thinner at the edges), bare bright metal rubbed through within 2 cm of a metal edge. Written into the g-buffer's albedo / roughness / metalness, so direct light, the bounce, the reflections and their highlights all answer to it. 0 = the g-buffer exactly as it was; 0.35 = lived-in; 1 = as far as it goes (?detail=)

label: character materials
title: each man shaded per material SLOT (skin, two cloths, webbing, boot, helmet, dark metal, rubber, lens, a marking) out of a table per side — operators one dark issue with hard kit that takes a highlight and their pair's colour as a band, defenders each in his own shirt, trousers and head, soft and dusty — with creases / ridges from the mesh's own curvature and the ground's dust up from the sole; bounce light and reflections see one colour per body part. Off = the two tints, the frame as it was. With the shipped mannequin the slots are a STAND-IN dealt by joint (?charmats); a mesh whose materials are named after the slots turns this on by itself (?nocharmats holds it off)

extra: off (two tints) · slots from the mesh's materials · slot sha

label: reproject with motion vectors
title: the g-buffer's per-pixel object motion (TAAU's gVel) added to the camera reprojection: a walking man's lit side and the bounce on him find their own history. Off = camera-only reprojection; needs TAAU on (the vectors are written for its resolve)

label: histories
extra: [restart — zero every screen-space history (the denoiser's, the reflection chain's, the TAAU resolve's, the ReSTIR reservoirs): the next frame starts from raw estimates (the same button as Frame ▸ Quality & resolution ▸ histories)]

label: shadow: à-trous iterations
title: strides 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 — 3 travel 7 px (the 10-px penumbra cap's worth); the preset sets it (ultra 4 · high / medium 3 · low / verylow 2)

label: shadow: history cap (frames)
title: the visibility ratio accumulates at α = 1/n up to this many frames (0 = no temporal reuse); what this frame's neighbourhood cannot see is clamped out at once whatever the cap (preset: ultra 16 · high 12 · medium 10 · low / verylow 8)

label: shadow: clamp k (σ)
title: history is held inside the current 5×5 neighbourhood's mean ± k·σ per class: small = responsive (moving shadows trail less) but noisier, large = smoother but laggier

label: shadow: luminance edge-stop σ_l
title: à-trous tap weight exp(−|Δ| / (σ_l·σ + ε)): differences the pixel's own noise explains are averaged, larger ones kept as edges (SVGF). Higher = smoother, lower = crisper contact shadows

label: shadow: moving-light history (frames, 0 = cue off)
title: the light-motion cue: a class whose exact UNSHADOWED luminance at the pixel changed by more than the threshold below since last frame (a torch sweeping, a switch, a flicker — the only way a still receiver's shadows of that class can have moved) accumulates over at most this many frames instead of the cap: responsive under moving light, long and smooth under still light. 0 = the long history everywhere

label: shadow: light-motion threshold
title: relative change of the class's unshadowed luminance per frame at which the moving history begins (fully in force at 3× this)

label: shadow: light-JUMP reset (rel. change, 0 = off)
title: a class whose unshadowed luminance at the pixel changed by more than this fraction of itself within ONE frame — a switch, a fluorescent tube's dropout strokes, a lightning stroke arriving — takes its value from that frame alone (bright outliers capped, leant on its 5×5 mean) and carries its sample VARIANCE across instead of booking the step as variance: the ratio S/U in that light's own shadows is another number after the jump, and letting the à-trous see the step as noise blurred every shadow the light casts into its surround for a dozen frames a stroke — shadows that pumped with the flicker (docs/internal/tjank.md). Keyed on the light the pixel believes visible (ReSTIR: U.a), not on a lamp behind the wall. 0 = the 08-11 behaviour

label: shadow: PCSS hint prior (kernel reach ≤ penumbra width)
title: each iteration only takes a pixel as far as its own / inherited blocker-distance penumbra width asks (softblur's contact hardening); off = pure variance guidance

label: shadow: lit-alike tap weight
title: taps weigh min(U)/max(U): ratios never mix across a cone edge or between different light footprints (softblur's rule)

label: shadow: hidden lights stay hidden
title: a carried torch behind a wall is in the unshadowed light but in nobody's shadow rays; on = a tap or a history taken under another amount of that light is read as the light it stands for, off = ratios averaged across the hidden cone draw it faintly on the far side (?noleakfix)

label: gi: à-trous iterations
title: on the gather grid (⅓ / ½ res): strides 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (preset: ultra 5 · high 4 · medium / low 3 · verylow 2)

label: gi: history cap (frames)
title: the bounce accumulates at α = 1/n up to this (preset: 32 / 24 / 16 / 12 / 8); Indirect light ▸ Final gather ▸ "temporal accumulation" off = none

label: gi: clamp k (σ)
title: the long history is held inside ± k·σ (of the current 5×5) round the FAST history: small = a moved torch's bounce follows at once but boils more; large = calm but laggy

label: gi: fast history (frames)
title: ReLAX's trick: a short EMA the clamp box is centred on (kills the long history's lag without clamping to one raw frame); 0 = centre on the raw neighbourhood mean

label: spec: à-trous iterations
title: the glossy floors' / glass field (only while either is on): reach shrinks with mirror-likeness

label: spec: roughness stand-in
title: the gather-grid specular field has no per-pixel roughness (the RT reflection chain does: its rows are Materials ▸ RT reflections): 0 = mirror (reprojection by the virtual hit point, tight clamp, no blur) … 1 = rough (surface motion, wide)

label: geometry: plane-distance k
title: edge-stop on |plane distance| ÷ (z·k): a slanted floor is one surface, a desk top never joins the floor

label: glass panes
title: the level's glazing (in the office: conference partition, manager sidelight, every exterior window) as glass: what stands behind a pane is drawn as always (the pane is in no raster and no traced ray meets it) and composite lays over it the pane's tint (albedo^depth ÷ cos), a traced mirror image × Schlick Fresnel (n 1.5: 4 % square-on, most of it edge-on) through the gloss floors' specular texture + history + blur pass, the analytic glint of small emitters, and a dust glow where light lands ON the glass; the direct pass tints light that crossed a pane. Men see through it and do not hear through it. What a round or a blast does to a pane is not this switch: that is glass breaking (the cracks, the pieces, rounds passing through). OFF = no pane list at all: every glass box is an empty opening (the level as it was) — the CPU side (feet, sound, the crack stars) stays. Costs a slab test per listed pane per pixel in composite, ~3 rays per glass texel at gather res. (frame flag 268435456; ?noglass boots it off)

label: reflection strength
title: × the physical Fresnel mirror term (1 = as traced; the share taken out of the transmitted picture is capped at the physical value whatever this says)

label: tint depth
title: exponent on a pane's albedo per crossing (÷ cos of the crossing angle): 0 = perfectly clear, 1 = one pane, 3 = bottle glass

label: dust glow
title: × the grime film's albedo (0.035): how much a torch beam or a lit panel shows ON the glass itself (both faces; two strongest lights shadow-tested)

label: refraction
title: the view ray BENDS through every glass box by Snell's law — into the glass at the face it meets, across the box to the face it leaves by (a face past the critical angle mirrors it back inside instead), out again — and what shows through is read where the bent ray comes out behind the glass (screen space: the picture already shaded there; nothing nearer than the glass is ever read, the sky keeps the pixel's own). The tint deepens by Beer–Lambert with the glass actually crossed, a box's authored tint read as its transmittance square through its own thickness: a 12 mm pane square-on is tinted exactly as before and shifts nothing you can see, a graze shifts a pixel or two and tints by the slanting path, the water-cooler bottle (30 cm of it) bends the cabinet edge behind it by centimetres and reads denser toward its rims. One law for every Glass box, evaluated only on glass pixels (≈ +0.05 ms with the glazing filling the view). OFF = the old tint rule (albedo^(depth ÷ cos)) and the read under the pixel, byte for byte (?norefract boots it off)

label: index of refraction
title: n of the glass (1.5 soda-lime, 1.33 water, 2.4 diamond; 1.0 = no bending at all — the absorption stays by path length). One index for every glass box: the panes and the bottle alike

label: panes
extra: [crack test — star the pane under the cursor (or the nearest within 4 m of the aim point) as a round would: a hole, a frosted collar and a crack star ON the glass — the floor hears it; the decals ▸ clear button (or a restart) wipes them]
glass ▸ 22 panes (laminated: rounds stop, glass stays) · 0 c

label: decals
title: The marks the encounter leaves — bullet holes where rounds stop, the stun charge's scorch (and its splashes up the walls), boot scuffs on kicked leaves, the chip a ring knocks out of the plaster — kept in a 512-entry ring on the CPU (render/decals.ts), bucketed per 1 m cell, and drawn by the g-buffer's fragment stage into the albedo / normal it stores (decals.wgsl), so direct light, the bounce and the glossy floors all answer to them. Marks on doors and furniture ride the box. Off = nothing recorded or uploaded and frame flag 4194304 down: the g-buffer exactly as it was (?nodecals)

label: decals
extra: [spray test pattern — every kind the shader draws, on what the player is facing / standing on right now] [+100 random — a realistic mix (holes, chips, the odd scorch) shot from random points inside the building at random walls — for the cost measurement] [clear decals]
decals 0/512 · drawn 0 · cell entries 0 · busiest cell 0/48

label: GPU particles
title: sparks, debris chips, dust puffs and spent casings simulated in one compute pass (collide with the trace grid, lit by the light buffer + three shadow rays + the radiance cache) and splatted into the HDR target after the composite. Off = the CPU box sparks of game/sparks.ts exactly as they were and none of the new impact debris / dust / brass (?noparticles at boot)

label: CAP: births per frame
title: renderer v3 Phase 0 cap: at most this many particles are born a frame; emit records that do not fit wait in the queue for the next frames (chips / dust / brass dealt before sparks; a spark record shed after 6 frames of waiting), so a firefight's bursts spread over a few frames instead of flooding one. 6144 = the old ceiling (a whole short ring). Set by the quality preset (512 / 384 / 256 / 192 / 128)

extra: queue: 0 waiting (peak 0) · shed 0 stale sparks · cap 0/f

label: shadow rays (3 strongest lights)
title: each lit particle scores every light unshadowed through the reach masks, traces a shadow ray toward the three strongest and credits the rest at 35 %; off = all unshadowed and whole (for measuring what the rays cost)

label: sparks bounce off surfaces
